name: shipyard-retrieval
title: Coding sessions: finding the session that holds the answer

conditions.corpus: 32 real agent sessions on a public repository over a simulated three weeks, with 67 questions that the repository and its commit messages do not answer
conditions.held out: 30 questions, chosen by a hash of their ids
conditions.scoring: every session holding the answer among the first five returned; no model involved

summary: Each question is asked twice: once in the session's own terms, once paraphrased with none of its distinctive words. Exact terms favour keyword search; paraphrase is where it is weakest.

metrics.label: ctx, all questions, own terms and paraphrased
grep, all questions, own terms and paraphrased

baseline: ranked grep over the same transcript files: each session scored by how many of the question's words it contains, then by how often
bar: a difference counts only if a sign test on the paired held-out questions gives p below 0.05 (set in bench/head-to-head.md before the run)
meaning: ctx's search did not beat ranked grep at finding the right session here. In the session's own terms grep found more (26 against 20 of 30 held out; alone right on 8 questions against ctx's 2, sign test p = 0.11, so by the rule set beforehand the two are level). Paraphrased, both fail most of the time: neither keyword method copes when the question shares no distinctive word with the session. The corpus is small, 32 sessions, which suits scoring whole sessions the way this grep does; ctx ranks single turns. Whether an agent answers better with ctx than with grep is a separate measurement, not yet run.
